args.goal:
Step 0, before anything else: copy the seeded workspace into your current working
directory, then work there.

    cp -a <RUNS>/seed-copy/. .

Do not modify anything under that source path; copy from it and leave it untouched.

Implement SPEC.md completely.

`SPEC.md` is a specification for `tabula`, a dependency-free tabular-data toolkit: 48 numbered
requirements (R-01 .. R-48) grouped into 8 sections, one section per module. The package skeleton
in `tabula/` already declares every public name the spec promises, and every one of them raises
`NotImplementedError`. Replace them with real, working code, using the Python 3.11 standard
library and nothing else.

Write your own tests beside the seeded `tests/test_contract.py`, and leave `pytest tests/ -q`
green when you stop. `test_contract.py` only checks that the public names exist with the stated
signatures - it passes against the untouched stubs, so a green run of it alone proves nothing.
The tests that show your code works are the ones you write.

You are scored by a hidden acceptance suite you will never see, built from the requirement ids in
SPEC.md and calling only the public API named there. Every stated behaviour is fair game,
including the error cases and the edge cases: empty input, duplicate column names, ragged rows,
nulls, coercion failures, non-ASCII text and very large integers. So the spec text is the
contract, not your reading of what the toolkit ought to do - where the spec fixes an exact name,
signature, exception type, ordering or output string, match it exactly, and where it looks odd,
implement what it says.

There is more here than one agent can finish. The sections are separable on purpose; the
dependencies that do cross a boundary are listed under "Layout" in SPEC.md.
